hook_line: ANTHROPIC'S 'COMPUTE MULTIPLIERS' PUT THE AI INFRASTRUCTURE BOOM IN QUESTION

hook_stat.sub: Revenue Anthropic told investors it could generate from a given amount of computing power, as previously expected

stats.label: Revenue per $1 of compute and infrastructure expense in Q3 2026, up from $0.40 in Q1 2025
Disclosed contractual commitments, mostly for compute and infrastructure
Short-term compute that cost more than multi-year capacity, contributing to the Q3 dip

diaspora_bullets: Customer demand still exceeds the computing capacity Anthropic has available
Demand for AI services and demand for physical infrastructure may not grow as closely together as previously assumed
news_summary: Anthropic's IPO filing highlights compute multipliers — research advances that let its Claude models do more work with less computing power — with revenue per $1 of compute and infrastructure expense rising from $0.40 in Q1 2025 to $1.72 in Q3 2026.
payoff: Anthropic is not cutting back: customer demand still exceeds the computing capacity it has available.
